title: AI on the Defensive and Offensive: Securing Multi-Environment Networks from AI-Crafted Cyber Attacks
summary: Builds a mixed-environment dataset of real and machine-generated network traffic, then tests whether detectors trained on it hold up against attacks crafted the same way. Three SDV synthesizers generate the traffic side: CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN, each applied to IoTID-20 and UNSW-NB15.
evidence: to generate AI-based samples, we employ various techniques, including CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN; we apply these three models separately to both the IoTID-20 and UNSW-NB15 datasets

title: Data Generation using a Probabilistic Auto-Regressive Model for Student Exam Performance Analysis
summary: Generates PPG signals for students under exam stress, where the real recordings are few and the data is multivariate time series rather than flat tables. SDV's PAR algorithm is the generator, applied to the Wearable Exam Stress Dataset and described as the first use of PAR in this setting.
evidence: the PAR algorithm is newly employed for data generation in education; the PAR algorithm synthesizes data using multivariate and multi-type time-series data; applied to the Wearable Exam Stress Dataset

title: iCTGAN: An Attack Mitigation Technique for Random-vector Attack on Accelerometer-based Gait Authentication Systems
summary: Gait authentication systems can be defeated by random-vector attacks, and the defence proposed here is to widen the variance of the impostor samples the classifier trains against. iCTGAN is CTGAN applied to an impostor feature matrix, trained with Wasserstein loss to synthesise those samples.
evidence: section '3.4.2 Impostor CTGAN (iCTGAN)': the underlying structure of CTGAN uses fully connected networks in generator and critic; the networks were trained using Wasserstein GAN loss

title: A deep learning framework to generate synthetic mobility data
summary: Synthesises a mobility database in two parts, separating who the travellers are from where they go, because the joint distribution is too complex to learn at once. CTGAN learns the socioeconomic variables of the synthetic population and is sampled alongside an RNN that produces the location traces.
evidence: we sample synthetic population and location datasets separately after training CTGAN and RNN models; our CTGAN and RNN components include layer, batch, and epoch size parameters

title: Multi-Resolution Diffusion for Privacy-Sensitive Recommender Systems
summary: Proposes SDRM, a diffusion model for generating recommender interaction data without exposing the real users behind it. CTGAN is one of the tabular generators SDRM is measured against.
evidence: CTGAN is listed among the generative baselines; our method surpasses other tabular data generation methods in the evaluation
